characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2000FX TEM; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% ethanol at an applied potential of 25 V
characterization_methods.key_findings: BF images show nano-sized disc-like B2 particles in the α matrix after higher-temperature annealing; the Ni-free alloy follows the same trend as the Ni-containing sample.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterization of the ordered phases (B2 discs, κ-carbides).
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) — selected-area diffraction patterns (SADPs) and bright-field (BF) imaging

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss Sigma FE-SEM operated at 20 kV, fitted with high-speed X-ray EDS
characterization_methods.key_findings: Revealed coarse GB-B2 particles, B2 stringer bands and the γ+κ matrix morphologies.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens polished and etched in 5% nital solution
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructural observation and phase composition measurement.
characterization_methods.technique: Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM) with X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Nano-indenter; constant loading/unloading rate applied to phases and phase combinations
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Ni-free alloy at 900 °C: γ = 3.8 GPa, α = 2.9 GPa, γ + B2 = 7.2 GPa, α + B2 = 8.9 GPa; composite structures are markedly harder than the parent γ and α phases.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s−1 up to a maximum load of 10000 μN with a hold time of 20 s; each measurement repeated at least 25 times, in arrays of 50–70 indentations
characterization_methods.purpose: To determine the nano-hardness of individual phases (solution-treated γ and α, B2 stringer bands, micro-meter sized and nano-disk B2) and of phase combinations (γ + cuboid κ, γ + κ + microsized B2, γ + microsized B2, α + needle-shape κ, α + nano-disk B2).

analytical_models.equation_role: Used elastic constants C11 and C44 from the slope of acoustic branches in the [100] direction and C12 from the [111] direction (equations 1–3)
analytical_models.model_name: Sound velocity relations for elastic constants

analytical_models.equation_role: Orthorhombic and monoclinic lattice distortions used to determine C11, C12 and C44 from total-energy changes (equations 4–7)
analytical_models.model_note: E(δ)=E(0)+(C11−C12)Vδ^2+O(δ^4) for orthorhombic distortion; E(δ)=E(0)+½C44Vδ^2+O(δ^4) for monoclinic distortion.

analytical_models.equation_role: Computed bulk modulus B0, anisotropy factor C_a, shear modulus G and Young's moduli E100 and E111 (equations 8–12)
Rationalized increased hardness from nano-sized disc-like B2 in α: the increase in shear stress (Δτ) is proportional to the inverse of the precipitate diameter (Δτ ∝ R^−1.25)
analytical_models.model_note: Smaller precipitate size increases resistance to shear, explaining higher hardness at higher annealing temperatures.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Brillouin zone integration with an 18×18×18 Monkhorst-Pack grid for structure optimization; real-space grid with 50 Ryd energy cut-off for charge density; augmentation charges expanded to 600 Ryd; a 30×30×30 grid with 60 Ryd cut-off used for electronic density of states and formation energy calculations; bulk modulus obtained by fitting simulated unit-cell volumes with a Murnaghan equation of state; dynamical matrices from linear response in the harmonic approximation; density of states by the tetrahedron method with a 30×30×30 mesh.
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: GGA Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) exchange-correlation functional, spin-polarized; ultrasoft pseudo-potentials based on modified Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos (RRKJ) scheme
computational_details.simulation_method: Density Functional Theory (DFT) ab-initio calculations (Hohenberg-Kohn formalism)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated lattice parameters of ordered precipitates (e.g. FeAl-B2) were slightly less than experimental values but in good agreement; the calculated lattice constant of Fe3AlC was larger than Fe3Al-L12, matching experimental observations; enrichment of κ-phase with Mn increased calculated bulk/shear/Young's moduli, consistent with the experimentally observed increase in hardness.

interfaces.interface_notes: In the present study B2 formed in the γ-phase with flat interfaces and sharp edges (average size ≈1.4 μm) and as disk-like precipitates (a few hundred nm) in α (b0026).
interfaces.phase_evolution: At 900–1050 °C B2 forms as micron-sized particles and grain-boundary precipitates in γ and as nano-sized discs in the ferrite (α); in the Ni-free alloy at 900 °C the B2 is FeAl-type and κ-carbides are absent.
interfaces.slip_behavior: The increase in shear resistance is attributed to uniformly distributed nano-sized disc-like B2 particles in the α matrix following the Orowan mechanism (Δτ ∝ R^−1.25), i.e. decreasing precipitate size increases resistance to shear.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Experimental alloys were melted in an induction furnace (both grades).
Solution heat-treated for 35 min at 1250 °C in a protective argon atmosphere and then water quenched; this is the parent process (proc_solution-treated-1250c-35min-wq) of the 900 °C annealing.
Materials cut into 3-mm (length), 3-mm (width) and 1-mm (thickness) samples for nano-indentation.
Annealing treatments conducted at 500, 700, 900 and 1050 °C; holding time not explicitly reported. Same annealing treatment applied to both alloys.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Nano-indentation at a constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s−1 up to a maximum load of 10000 μN with a hold time of 20 s; each measurement in a particular phase repeated at least 25 times in arrays of 50–70 indentations.

precipitates.distribution: in γ matrix and at grain boundaries

structures.overall_structure: Duplex γ + α microstructure of the Ni-free Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C steel after annealing at 900 °C. The austenite (γ) matrix contains coarse B2 particles (2–4 μm) and grain-boundary B2, while the ferrite (α) contains disc-like B2 precipitates (≈200 nm); no κ-carbides at this temperature.

unmapped_findings: For the Ni-free alloy at 900 °C the Al content of the B2 particles in α (nanosized B2) was ~22.9 wt.% and of the coarse FeAl-type B2 particles in γ was ~18.3 wt.%; b0029 states the Al content of the particles ranged from 22.8 to 24.6 wt.% for the 900–1050 °C treatments.

The nanoindentation technique used in this study could not measure isolated nano-sized precipitates; it measured a compound hardness of the matrix together with the nano-sized features (compound values), so individual nano-particle hardness could not be resolved (b0026, b0042).

The coarse B2 phase formed in γ was reported with flat interfaces and sharp edges with an average size of ≈1.4 μm (b0026), whereas Table 1 lists coarse B2 particles of 2–4 μm for the Ni-free alloy at 900 °C (b0022).
The annealing holding time for the 900 °C treatment is not explicitly reported in the paper (b0017).
The paper labels the same Ni-free alloy both as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C (text) and as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C (Tables 1 and 2), an apparent typographical inconsistency (b0017, b0022, b0032).
